text.p: Earnings estimates for French carmakers Peugeot and Renault were raised at JP Morgan on Friday, due to the positive impact on profits of the sharp rise in sterling, the investment bank said.

For Renault, JP Morgan analysts upgraded their 1997 net profit estimates to a profit of 1.2 billion francs from a loss of 1.1 billion, and the 1998 net profit forecast to 3.1 billion francs from 0.6 billion.
For Peugeot, the investment bank upgraded its 1997 net profit estimate to a profit of 0.36 billion francs from a loss of 0.45 bilion and raised its 1998 profit figure to 1.9 billion from 0.9 billion.
JP Morgan continued to rate both as "market performers", arguing that they face stragegic problems in a European car industry where broader difficulties are likely to continue.
